theme: Every Name Counts on the Team
hindi: दुर्योधन द्रोणाचार्य को पांडवों की सेना के और वीरों के नाम बताता है: पराक्रमी युधामन्यु, बलवान उत्तमौजा, सुभद्रा का पुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पुत्र। ये सभी महारथी हैं।
english: Duryodhana keeps pointing out the Pandava warriors to Drona: brave Yudhamanyu, strong Uttamauja, Subhadra’s son Abhimanyu, and the sons of Draupadi. All of them, he says, are maharathas, great chariot-warriors.
deeper: This verse is another part of Duryodhana’s list. He is naming the brave people on the other side, one after another. Notice that he does not call them weak. He calls every one of them vikrānta (brave), vīryavān (strong) and mahāratha (great warrior). Inside, Duryodhana is counting, and the count is making him nervous.

The names in this verse include some very young people. Abhimanyu was Arjuna’s teenage son, and the sons of Draupadi were also young. A good army has experienced elders and fresh young fighters together. Everyone has a place, and a team is strong when every member, big or small, is counted.

The gentle lesson for us is about how fear feels. When we are worried, we start counting the other side’s strengths again and again, and the worry grows. The Gita will slowly teach Arjuna, and us, to stay steady and look at our duty clearly, not just at the numbers.
words: Yudhamanyu, a warrior prince of the Panchala side
son of Subhadra, that is Abhimanyu
background: The great war of Kurukshetra is about to begin. Duryodhana goes to his teacher Drona and tells him to look at the Pandava army, which was arranged by Drona’s own clever student, the son of Drupada (1.3). He then names mighty archers who are equal to Bhima and Arjuna, such as Yuyudhana, Virata and Drupada (1.4).

He keeps going with the list: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya (1.5). In this verse (1.6) he adds Yudhamanyu, Uttamauja, Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi, and says all of them are maharathas.
lessons: A team is made of many people, young and old, and each one adds strength.
Young people can be brave too
Abhimanyu and Draupadi’s sons were young, yet they were counted among great warriors.
When we are worried, we keep listing the other side’s strengths and forget our own.
Even Duryodhana had to admit that the other side’s warriors were brave and strong.
Numbers and names do not decide everything; a calm mind and clear duty matter more.
examples: Aarav is the youngest player in the school football team. His captain says, “We need you too.” Aarav feels proud because every player counts, not only the tall ones.
In the Annual Day play, Meera only has to hold the curtain rope. Without her, the play cannot start. Every small job is part of the big success.
Before the quiz, Kabir keeps listing how many clever kids are in the other house. His stomach feels tight. He realises that counting rivals only makes him more scared, so he goes back to revising.
Ananya loses the race to Priya. She still says, “You ran really fast!” Giving honest credit to someone else is a sign of a big heart.
Ten-year-old Rohan helps his grandmother use her new phone. Even though he is small, he is the expert in the house today. Age does not decide who can help.
Sara knows that the other cricket team practises every evening. Instead of worrying, she decides to practise her own bowling a bit longer. Noticing strength in others can push us to work harder.
During Swachh Bharat week, every child in class 5B picks a small task: sweeping, watering plants, collecting paper. The school ground shines because nobody was left out.
At Diwali, Dadi makes sweets, Papa hangs lights, Mummy draws rangoli, and little Ishaan arranges the diyas. The festival is beautiful because each person did a part.

story.title: Abhimanyu and the Secret of the Chakravyuha
paras: Abhimanyu was the son of Arjuna and Subhadra, and he is one of the warriors named in this verse. There is a well-known tale that, while he was still in his mother’s womb, his father was telling Subhadra how to break into a chakravyuha, a spinning circle-shaped battle formation.
Arjuna explained how to enter the circle. But before he reached the part about how to come out, Subhadra fell asleep. So the baby Abhimanyu heard only half of the secret.

Years later, on the thirteenth day of the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas were challenged with this very formation. Young Abhimanyu bravely said that he knew how to enter it. He went in with great courage and fought like a true maharatha, but he did not know the way out, and he was lost in the battle.

The Pandavas and their friends were deeply sad. People remember Abhimanyu even today for his courage at such a young age. They also remember how important it is to listen to a lesson all the way to the end.
story.moral: Lesson: Young people can be very brave, and we should learn things completely, listening until the end.

quiz.q: Who is Abhimanyu in this verse called by the name Saubhadra?
quiz.x: Saubhadra means the son of Subhadra, who is Abhimanyu.

quiz.q: What does the word mahā-rathāḥ mean?
quiz.x: Mahā means great and rathī means chariot-warrior, so mahārathas are great warriors.

quiz.q: Who is Duryodhana speaking to while naming these warriors?
quiz.x: Duryodhana is pointing out the Pandava heroes to his teacher Drona.

quiz.q: What gentle lesson does this list of names teach us?
o: Every team member counts, young or old
quiz.x: The verse names young and old warriors alike, showing that every member adds to a team’s strength.

reel.hook: Can a teenager be counted among great warriors? The Gita says yes!
reel.lesson: Every member of a team counts, whether young or old, small or tall.
reel.caption:
Even the youngest ones get a place on the team 🏹 Abhimanyu was counted among the great warriors, so never think you are too small to matter.
Who is the youngest member of your family team? 💛
